butyrate-cell-energy.subject: butyrate
butyrate-cell-energy.text: Butyrate restored mitochondrial respiration in colonocytes from germ-free mice.
butyrate-cell-energy.limitations: This experiment examines mouse cell energy metabolism, not symptom improvement in people.

fibre-capacity.subject: fibre
fibre-capacity.text: The high-fibre dietary arm increased microbial carbohydrate-degrading capacity while overall diversity stayed stable.
fibre-capacity.limitations: A microbiome measurement is not a demonstrated treatment effect. Responses differed between participants.

fermented-diversity.subject: fermented-food-diet
fermented-diversity.text: A mixed fermented-food diet increased microbial diversity and reduced several inflammatory markers in the trial.
fermented-diversity.limitations: The intervention combined foods. It does not isolate yoghurt or establish disease treatment.

yoghurt-digestion.subject: yoghurt
yoghurt-digestion.text: Lactase-deficient participants digested lactose in yoghurt better than the comparison lactose loads.
yoghurt-digestion.limitations: A result about lactose digestion cannot establish that every fermented food has the same effect.

microbes-serotonin.subject: gut
microbes-serotonin.text: Spore-forming communities altered host serotonin production and related physiology in experimental models.
microbes-serotonin.limitations: Gut serotonin regulation does not demonstrate delivery of serotonin into the brain or a treatment for depression.

gut-neural-circuit.subject: neuropod-cells
gut-neural-circuit.text: Mouse enteroendocrine neuropod cells transmitted nutrient-related signals to vagal neurons using glutamate.
gut-neural-circuit.limitations: This specific neural route does not explain every form of gut–brain communication.

mood-association.subject: faecalibacterium
mood-association.text: Faecalibacterium and Coprococcus were associated with quality-of-life measures in human cohorts.
mood-association.limitations: An association does not establish that adding these organisms improves mood.

mouse-behaviour.subject: bacteroides-fragilis
mouse-behaviour.text: B. fragilis treatment changed permeability and some behavioural measures in the studied mouse model.
mouse-behaviour.limitations: This was not a trial treating autism in people.

exercise-microbiome.subject: movement
exercise-microbiome.text: Exercise-related microbial changes depend on the protocol, population and measurement.
exercise-microbiome.limitations: The studies used different protocols and populations; they are not interchangeable replications.

testing-scope.subject: gut
testing-scope.text: Microbiome testing requires a defined clinical question, appropriate methods and evidence of usefulness.
testing-scope.limitations: An organism percentage alone does not establish disease or an effective treatment.

step:living-well:fibre:0.subject: fibre
step:living-well:fibre:0.text: Beans, oats, vegetables and whole grains supply carbohydrates that escape digestion in the small intestine. The structure of a fibre shapes which microbes can start breaking it down.
step:living-well:fibre:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:fibre:1.subject: starch
step:living-well:fibre:1.text: Ruminococcus bromii can attach to resistant starch and begin dismantling it. Other organisms gain access to released sugars, making starch degradation a shared activity.
step:living-well:fibre:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:fibre:2.subject: bifidobacterium
step:living-well:fibre:2.text: Bifidobacteria produce acetate and lactate. Some neighbouring bacteria consume these products and generate butyrate. A meal supports a network of transactions.
step:living-well:fibre:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:fibre:3.subject: butyrate
step:living-well:fibre:3.text: Butyrate is an important fuel for cells lining the colon. Its effects on metabolism and immune signalling connect microbial fermentation to the tissue that houses it.
step:living-well:fibre:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:fermented:0.subject: milk
step:living-well:fermented:0.text: Yoghurt, cabbage ferments and tempeh begin with different ingredients and communities. Their fermentation changes acidity, texture and food chemistry.
step:living-well:fermented:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:fermented:1.subject: gut
step:living-well:fermented:1.text: In a randomised study of 36 healthy adults, the fermented-food arm increased gut microbial diversity and reduced several inflammatory markers. Participants ate a mixture of foods.
step:living-well:fermented:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:fermented:2.subject: soybeans
step:living-well:fermented:2.text: Live-culture yoghurt, a baked loaf and cooked tempeh deliver different mixtures of living microbes, microbial products and transformed ingredients. Fermentation continues to matter after organisms are killed by cooking.
step:living-well:fermented:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:movement:0.subject: movement
step:living-well:movement:0.text: Movement changes circulation, energy use and intestinal physiology. Exercise studies measure how the microbial community responds alongside the person.
step:living-well:movement:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:movement:1.subject: movement
step:living-well:movement:1.text: Previously sedentary adults completed supervised endurance training. Short-chain fatty acids increased in lean participants, with a different response in participants with obesity.
step:living-well:movement:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:movement:2.subject: movement
step:living-well:movement:2.text: A separate three-week interval-training study found better fitness without a detectable change in bacterial composition. Duration, activity and the initial community help define the question.
step:living-well:movement:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:sleep:0.subject: sleep
step:living-well:sleep:0.text: Researchers compared adequate sleep with severe restriction while controlling diet and activity in healthy young men. This makes sleep itself an experimental variable.
step:living-well:sleep:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:sleep:1.subject: sleep
step:living-well:sleep:1.text: After three restricted nights, microbial richness fell, while other diversity measures and intestinal permeability were unchanged. The gut responds along several distinct dimensions.
step:living-well:sleep:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:mood:0.subject: tryptophan
step:living-well:mood:0.text: The gut and brain exchange information through sensory nerves, circulating precursors, immune responses and microbial metabolites. Serotonin can activate a gut sensory fibre whose electrical signal travels toward the brainstem. Human studies then ask how particular changes relate to mood, stress and quality of life.
step:living-well:mood:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:mood:1.subject: bifidobacterium
step:living-well:mood:1.text: In a small study of healthy volunteers, Bifidobacterium longum 1714 was associated with reduced stress responses and subtle memory changes. The study followed one strain through defined measurements.
step:living-well:mood:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:digestion:0.subject: fibre
step:living-well:digestion:0.text: As gut contents move, nutrients are used up and microbial products accumulate. Transit time helps determine the environment encountered by successive communities.
step:living-well:digestion:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:digestion:1.subject: gut
step:living-well:digestion:1.text: A study connecting colonic transit with microbial metabolism found that time in the colon was related to the balance of fermentation and protein breakdown. Stool measurements are part of that moving system.
step:living-well:digestion:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:resistant-starch:0.subject: starch
step:living-well:resistant-starch:0.text: Starch digestibility depends on its plant structure and preparation. Resistant fractions reach the colon, where specialist organisms can attach to and break apart the starch granules.
step:living-well:resistant-starch:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:resistant-starch:1.subject: ruminococcus-bromii
step:living-well:resistant-starch:1.text: In laboratory communities, Ruminococcus bromii unlocks resistant starch for other bacteria. Its activity changes who can use the food and which fermentation products become available.
step:living-well:resistant-starch:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:resistant-starch:2.subject: acetate
step:living-well:resistant-starch:2.text: Released carbohydrates support other fermenters. Acetate and lactate can then feed butyrate producers, connecting the initial starch degraders to the wider community.
step:living-well:resistant-starch:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:pulses:0.subject: protein
step:living-well:pulses:0.text: Pulses contain protein, starch and fermentable carbohydrates. Our enzymes digest part of the meal; the remaining carbohydrates supply organisms further down the gut.
step:living-well:pulses:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:pulses:1.subject: bifidobacterium
step:living-well:pulses:1.text: Bifidobacteria ferment carbohydrates into products including acetate and lactate. Other bacteria can use these products, extending the food web beyond the first consumer.
step:living-well:pulses:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:pulses:2.subject: fibre
step:living-well:pulses:2.text: The Stanford diet intervention tracked changes over weeks. Increasing fibre changed microbial carbohydrate-processing capacity; microbial diversity did not rise across the entire high-fibre group.
step:living-well:pulses:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:breakfast:0.subject: fibre
step:living-well:breakfast:0.text: Oats and fruit contribute a mixture of fibres. Microbes differ in their ability to use these structures, so a mixed meal offers more than a single purified substrate.
step:living-well:breakfast:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:breakfast:1.subject: lactose
step:living-well:breakfast:1.text: Yoghurt cultures ferment milk before it reaches the gut. Their lactase activity can improve digestion of the yoghurt’s lactose in people who digest lactose poorly.
step:living-well:breakfast:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:breakfast:2.subject: fibre
step:living-well:breakfast:2.text: The fermented-food arm of the Stanford trial increased microbial diversity and reduced several inflammatory markers. Participants ate a range of fermented foods, so the result describes that dietary pattern.
step:living-well:breakfast:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:oral-care:0.subject: streptococcus-thermophilus
step:living-well:oral-care:0.text: Dental plaque is an attached microbial community. Food, saliva and the tooth surface create local environments that differ from the surrounding mouth.
step:living-well:oral-care:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:oral-care:1.subject: streptococcus-thermophilus
step:living-well:oral-care:1.text: Sugar fermentation lowers plaque pH. Repeated acid exposure favours acid-tolerant organisms and removes minerals from tooth enamel.
step:living-well:oral-care:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:oral-care:2.subject: lactate
step:living-well:oral-care:2.text: Cleaning plaque, using fluoride toothpaste and reducing frequent sugary snacks change the conditions in which the oral community lives. The goal is a stable tooth-supporting habitat.
step:living-well:oral-care:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:daily-eating-windows:0.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:daily-eating-windows:0.text: A controlled feeding trial varied carbohydrate content and daily eating windows within calorie restriction. It tracked body composition together with microbial and metabolite measurements.
step:living-well:daily-eating-windows:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:daily-eating-windows:1.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:daily-eating-windows:1.text: In a three-month trial, early and late windows produced different changes in diversity measures and some bacterial genera. Overall between-group community differences were not significant.
step:living-well:daily-eating-windows:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:daily-eating-windows:2.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:daily-eating-windows:2.text: A larger multicentre trial compared early, late and self-selected windows with Mediterranean-diet education alone. The extra time restriction did not produce a significant between-group difference in liver outcomes or measured stool microbiota.
step:living-well:daily-eating-windows:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:longer-fasts:0.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:longer-fasts:0.text: A trial substudy compared a five-day fast followed by modified DASH eating with the diet alone. Blood pressure, medication need and body-mass index were lower in the fasting programme at three months.
step:living-well:longer-fasts:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:longer-fasts:1.subject: gut
step:living-well:longer-fasts:1.text: The same substudy measured changes in taxa and gene modules linked to short-chain-fatty-acid production. These exploratory measurements connect the clinical result to possible biological routes.
step:living-well:longer-fasts:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:living-well:longer-fasts:2.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:longer-fasts:2.text: A mouse experiment transferred microbes from fasting donors and reduced autoimmune disease in recipients. Its accompanying human pilot measured microbial and blood changes. These are distinct steps toward testing a treatment.
step:living-well:longer-fasts:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:yoghurt:0.subject: milk
step:fermentation:yoghurt:0.text: Streptococcus thermophilus and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus grow together in milk. Each changes the conditions and nutrients available to its partner.
step:fermentation:yoghurt:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:yoghurt:1.subject: lactose
step:fermentation:yoghurt:1.text: The bacteria ferment lactose to lactic acid. As acidity rises, milk proteins assemble into a gel that traps water.
step:fermentation:yoghurt:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:yoghurt:2.subject: milk
step:fermentation:yoghurt:2.text: Cooling slows further fermentation. Refrigerated live-culture yoghurt contains the transformed milk and its starter organisms. Heating after fermentation changes that living population.
step:fermentation:yoghurt:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:yoghurt:3.subject: lactose
step:fermentation:yoghurt:3.text: Microbial lactase in yoghurt helps digest its lactose. Fermented milk is one of the foods included in human diet interventions, where the whole dietary pattern is measured.
step:fermentation:yoghurt:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:sauerkraut:0.subject: cabbage
step:fermentation:sauerkraut:0.text: Salt draws liquid from shredded cabbage. Keeping the cabbage beneath its brine creates conditions favouring lactic acid bacteria.
step:fermentation:sauerkraut:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:sauerkraut:1.subject: cabbage
step:fermentation:sauerkraut:1.text: Leuconostoc and other lactic acid bacteria use cabbage sugars. Acid and gas change the vessel, and the community shifts as the environment becomes more acidic.
step:fermentation:sauerkraut:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:sauerkraut:2.subject: cabbage
step:fermentation:sauerkraut:2.text: Acid-tolerant bacteria continue the transformation. Temperature affects its pace: the USDA method gives about three to four weeks at 21–24°C.
step:fermentation:sauerkraut:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:sauerkraut:3.subject: cabbage
step:fermentation:sauerkraut:3.text: Refrigeration slows microbial activity. Canning heats the finished food, preserving the acidified cabbage while reducing its living microbial population.
step:fermentation:sauerkraut:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:tempeh:0.subject: soybeans
step:fermentation:tempeh:0.text: Cooked soybeans provide a moist, nutrient-rich surface for a Rhizopus starter. This is a solid-state fermentation.
step:fermentation:tempeh:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:tempeh:1.subject: rhizopus
step:fermentation:tempeh:1.text: Rhizopus grows branching filaments between the beans. The growing mycelium binds them into a coherent cake.
step:fermentation:tempeh:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:tempeh:2.subject: rhizopus
step:fermentation:tempeh:2.text: Fungal enzymes break down components of the beans, changing texture, flavour and nutrient accessibility. Starter and substrate both shape the result.
step:fermentation:tempeh:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:tempeh:3.subject: soybeans
step:fermentation:tempeh:3.text: Tempeh is commonly cooked before eating. The meal delivers a transformed protein-rich food; its value does not depend on the fungus remaining alive in the gut.
step:fermentation:tempeh:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kefir:0.subject: milk
step:fermentation:kefir:0.text: Kefir grains carry bacteria and yeasts in a shared matrix. Adding them to milk introduces a mixed community.
step:fermentation:kefir:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kefir:1.subject: lactobacillus
step:fermentation:kefir:1.text: Different members grow and exchange metabolites over the course of fermentation. Their activity produces acids, gas and flavour compounds.
step:fermentation:kefir:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kefir:2.subject: milk
step:fermentation:kefir:2.text: Removing the grains separates the reusable culture from the fermented drink. Cooling slows subsequent activity.
step:fermentation:kefir:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kefir:3.subject: milk
step:fermentation:kefir:3.text: The finished food combines fermented milk, microbial products and living organisms. Grain composition explains some differences between batches.
step:fermentation:kefir:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kimchi:0.subject: cabbage
step:fermentation:kimchi:0.text: Vegetables supply carbohydrates and their surface communities; salt and seasonings shape the starting conditions.
step:fermentation:kimchi:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kimchi:1.subject: cabbage
step:fermentation:kimchi:1.text: Lactic acid bacteria produce organic acids and other flavour compounds as the vegetables ferment.
step:fermentation:kimchi:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kimchi:2.subject: leuconostoc
step:fermentation:kimchi:2.text: Storage temperature and time change the balance of organisms and the sourness of the food.
step:fermentation:kimchi:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kimchi:3.subject: cabbage
step:fermentation:kimchi:3.text: Kimchi is one of several fermented vegetables included in human dietary intervention research.
step:fermentation:kimchi:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:sourdough:0.subject: grain
step:fermentation:sourdough:0.text: Flour and water supply nutrients to a community of yeasts and bacteria. Refreshing it provides another supply of substrate.
step:fermentation:sourdough:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:sourdough:1.subject: grain
step:fermentation:sourdough:1.text: Yeasts and some bacteria generate gas; lactic acid bacteria acidify the dough. The community changes flavour and structure.
step:fermentation:sourdough:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:sourdough:2.subject: grain
step:fermentation:sourdough:2.text: Heat sets the loaf and kills most starter organisms. The transformed grain and fermentation products remain part of the food.
step:fermentation:sourdough:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:sourdough:3.subject: grain
step:fermentation:sourdough:3.text: A baked sourdough loaf contributes to a meal through its ingredients and fermentation history. Whole-grain content changes its fibre contribution.
step:fermentation:sourdough:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:miso:0.subject: grain
step:fermentation:miso:0.text: Aspergillus oryzae grows on cooked grain and produces enzymes that break larger food molecules into smaller ones.
step:fermentation:miso:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:miso:1.subject: soybeans
step:fermentation:miso:1.text: Koji enzymes act in the soybean mixture, releasing sugars and amino acids.
step:fermentation:miso:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:miso:2.subject: soybeans
step:fermentation:miso:2.text: Salt-tolerant yeasts and bacteria join ongoing enzyme activity during maturation. A study of spontaneous nesashi miso found a different fungal community, led by Mucor, from the koji-based misos used for comparison.
step:fermentation:miso:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:miso:3.subject: soybeans
step:fermentation:miso:3.text: Miso adds fermented flavour in a concentrated salty ingredient. Heating changes the living population while preserving much of the food’s flavour.
step:fermentation:miso:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kombucha:0.subject: tea
step:fermentation:kombucha:0.text: Yeasts split sugar and produce ethanol and carbon dioxide. Acetic-acid bacteria use that ethanol near the oxygen-rich surface. The floating cellulose layer houses part of the community; the starter liquid also carries living organisms.
step:fermentation:kombucha:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kombucha:1.subject: ethanol
step:fermentation:kombucha:1.text: As fermentation proceeds, organic acids accumulate and sweetness changes. The University of Georgia method uses a breathable cover and a measured starter acidity. Time alone does not describe the state of a ferment.
step:fermentation:kombucha:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:kombucha:2.subject: acetate
step:fermentation:kombucha:2.text: Refrigeration slows the community. Sugar, caffeine, alcohol and acids remain in amounts that vary between batches. Enjoy kombucha as a fermented drink; its composition is a separate question from whether it changes a particular health outcome.
step:fermentation:kombucha:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:water-kefir:0.subject: sugar
step:fermentation:water-kefir:0.text: Water-kefir grains contain bacteria and yeasts embedded in a polysaccharide matrix. They are a different culture from milk-kefir grains and grow in a sugar-water medium.
step:fermentation:water-kefir:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:water-kefir:1.subject: sugar
step:fermentation:water-kefir:1.text: Lactic-acid bacteria, yeasts and acetic-acid bacteria share the available substrates. Their products include organic acids, carbon dioxide and ethanol. Culture and conditions shape the finished drink.
step:fermentation:water-kefir:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:water-kefir:2.subject: lactate
step:fermentation:water-kefir:2.text: Straining separates the grains from the drink so the culture can start another batch. The liquid remains biologically active, and its residual sugar and alcohol vary.
step:fermentation:water-kefir:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:dill-pickles:0.subject: leuconostoc
step:fermentation:dill-pickles:0.text: The USDA procedure combines pickling cucumbers, salt, water, dill and a measured amount of vinegar. The proportions establish the starting environment for fermentation.
step:fermentation:dill-pickles:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:dill-pickles:1.subject: leuconostoc
step:fermentation:dill-pickles:1.text: Lactic-acid bacteria consume vegetable sugars while the cucumbers remain submerged. Acidity increases, flavour develops and the brine becomes cloudy.
step:fermentation:dill-pickles:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:dill-pickles:2.subject: fibre
step:fermentation:dill-pickles:2.text: Refrigeration slows fermentation. Heat processing creates a different stored product and reduces the living microbial population. The food still contains the acids and transformed vegetable tissue.
step:fermentation:dill-pickles:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:fermented-carrots:0.subject: leuconostoc
step:fermentation:fermented-carrots:0.text: Carrot sticks supply sugars and a firm plant structure. A wet brine surrounds the pieces; a food-safe weight keeps them beneath the surface.
step:fermentation:fermented-carrots:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:fermented-carrots:1.subject: leuconostoc
step:fermentation:fermented-carrots:1.text: Vegetable-associated lactic-acid bacteria ferment available sugars. As acids accumulate, the environment favours organisms that tolerate sour conditions. Salt, temperature and submersion shape the process.
step:fermentation:fermented-carrots:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:fermentation:fermented-carrots:2.subject: fibre
step:fermentation:fermented-carrots:2.text: The finished carrots bring acidity, texture and plant fibre to the plate. A small serving can accompany beans, grains or sandwiches. Refrigeration slows further change.
step:fermentation:fermented-carrots:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:0.subject: helicobacter
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:0.text: Helicobacter pylori reaches the stomach and establishes a long-lived association with the gastric lining. In many people infection persists for years.
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:1.subject: helicobacter
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:1.text: Local changes in acidity alter the properties of gastric mucus. Experiments show H. pylori using this change to move through a material that otherwise restricts its movement.
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:2.subject: urea
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:2.text: A gated urea channel supplies substrate to urease. Urea is converted into ammonia and carbon dioxide, helping the bacterium manage its acidic surroundings.
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:3.subject: helicobacter
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:3.text: Persistent infection drives inflammation in the stomach lining. Long-term eradication studies examine outcomes including gastric cancer, linking microbial persistence to disease prevention.
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:4.subject: helicobacter
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:4.text: Breath testing and stool antigen testing detect active infection. The 2024 ACG adult guideline recommends bismuth quadruple therapy when susceptibility is unknown and advises against empiric clarithromycin triple therapy. Local resistance and prior antibiotics shape the regimen.
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:4.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:5.subject: antibiotics
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:5.text: The ACG guideline calls for a test of cure at least four weeks after antibiotics, with acid-suppressing PPIs held for two weeks to reduce false negatives. Arrange the timing with the treating clinician.
step:illness-recovery:helicobacter:5.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:cdiff:0.subject: antibiotics
step:illness-recovery:cdiff:0.text: Antibiotic exposure can reduce competitors and change the resources and bile-acid environment in which C. difficile grows. Spores allow it to persist outside the body.
step:illness-recovery:cdiff:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:cdiff:1.subject: cdiff
step:illness-recovery:cdiff:1.text: Toxigenic C. difficile produces toxins A and B. Infection can inflame the colon and cause diarrhoea, fever and abdominal pain. A positive test without symptoms can instead represent colonisation.
step:illness-recovery:cdiff:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:cdiff:2.subject: cdiff
step:illness-recovery:cdiff:2.text: CDC describes oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin for confirmed infection. Testing is interpreted alongside diarrhoea and other clinical findings. Unnecessary repeat testing after symptoms resolve can remain positive.
step:illness-recovery:cdiff:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:cdiff:3.subject: gut
step:illness-recovery:cdiff:3.text: A randomised trial of an oral purified spore preparation reduced recurrence after standard antibiotics in adults with recurrent infection. This asks a different question from adding a supermarket probiotic.
step:illness-recovery:cdiff:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:norovirus:0.subject: norovirus
step:illness-recovery:norovirus:0.text: Norovirus spreads through contaminated food, water, surfaces and close contact. It infects people; gut bacteriophages infect bacteria.
step:illness-recovery:norovirus:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:norovirus:1.subject: norovirus
step:illness-recovery:norovirus:1.text: Human intestinal enteroid experiments let researchers grow norovirus in tissue derived from human intestinal cells and examine host factors and viral replication.
step:illness-recovery:norovirus:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:norovirus:2.subject: norovirus
step:illness-recovery:norovirus:2.text: Vomiting and diarrhoea can rapidly deplete fluid and salts. Oral rehydration replaces these losses; severe dehydration needs medical care.
step:illness-recovery:norovirus:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:norovirus:3.subject: hydration
step:illness-recovery:norovirus:3.text: Most illness resolves in one to three days. Viral shedding can continue after symptoms stop. CDC advises staying home for 48 hours after symptoms end, plus careful handwashing and cleaning.
step:illness-recovery:norovirus:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:giardia:0.subject: giardia
step:illness-recovery:giardia:0.text: Giardia cysts reach the gut through contaminated water, food or contact. The organism’s active form lives in the small intestine.
step:illness-recovery:giardia:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:giardia:1.subject: giardia
step:illness-recovery:giardia:1.text: Trophozoites attach at the intestinal surface. Infection can interfere with absorption and lead to diarrhoea, gas and bloating.
step:illness-recovery:giardia:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:giardia:2.subject: giardia
step:illness-recovery:giardia:2.text: Stool testing identifies the parasite. CDC lists tinidazole, nitazoxanide and metronidazole among effective medicines; hydration remains important during diarrhoea.
step:illness-recovery:giardia:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:giardia:3.subject: giardia
step:illness-recovery:giardia:3.text: Some people continue to have symptoms after Giardia has cleared. Follow-up of an outbreak found increased rates of IBS and fatigue years later. Repeat symptoms deserve assessment rather than automatic retreatment.
step:illness-recovery:giardia:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:0.subject: antibiotics
step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:0.text: Antibiotics change microbial populations beyond the organism targeted by treatment. The starting community and antibiotic exposure shape what follows.
step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:1.subject: bifidobacterium
step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:1.text: Surviving organisms grow into available niches. Introduced organisms interact with those survivors, so adding a preparation can change the recovery path.
step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:2.subject: gut
step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:2.text: In one human experiment, an 11-strain probiotic delayed return of the native mucosal community; autologous stool transfer accelerated it. The study measured community reconstitution after a specific antibiotic exposure.
step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:3.subject: fibre
step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:3.text: Eating and digestion are the practical context for recovery. Fermented foods are foods, while microbiome therapies for recurrent infection are clinical interventions with their own evidence.
step:illness-recovery:antibiotics:3.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:ongoing-symptoms:0.subject: gut
step:illness-recovery:ongoing-symptoms:0.text: Constipation, diarrhoea, pain and bloating can involve transit, fermentation, sensitivity and tissue inflammation. They are useful entrances into the atlas’s existing habitat research.
step:illness-recovery:ongoing-symptoms:0.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:ongoing-symptoms:1.subject: fibre
step:illness-recovery:ongoing-symptoms:1.text: Transit time changes the resources available to microbes. Fermentation products and host responses create additional paths to examine in a specific symptom pattern.
step:illness-recovery:ongoing-symptoms:1.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

step:illness-recovery:ongoing-symptoms:2.subject: gut
step:illness-recovery:ongoing-symptoms:2.text: After an infection, symptoms can persist beyond pathogen clearance. Research that measures symptoms alongside microbial functions helps separate recovery of the person from a single stool readout.
step:illness-recovery:ongoing-symptoms:2.limitations: Authored explanation; exact claim-to-result support awaits review.

varied-fibre-foods.subject: fibre
varied-fibre-foods.text: Choose several fibre sources: oats and other wholegrains, beans or lentils, vegetables, fruit, nuts and seeds.
varied-fibre-foods.limitations: General food guidance does not replace a plan for a particular condition or establish a benefit from targeting one microbe.

step:living-well:fasting:0.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:fasting:0.text: Ramadan daylight fasting includes abstaining from fluids, with eating after sunset and before dawn. Daily eating windows and alternate-day schedules use different rules. Ramadan stool studies report community shifts, but food, sleep and energy intake also change. Those observations cannot isolate a timing effect.
step:living-well:fasting:0.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:fasting:1.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:fasting:1.text: Across randomised trials, intermittent fasting generally produces metabolic and weight outcomes similar to continuous energy restriction. A 12-month trial found no significant extra benefit from an early eating window when both groups restricted calories. A separate programme combining fasting and protein pacing changed microbial profiles, but cannot isolate fasting from the protein intervention.
step:living-well:fasting:1.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:fasting:2.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:fasting:2.text: A small controlled-feeding crossover experiment in men with prediabetes found improved insulin sensitivity with early eating despite weight maintenance. This is evidence about a specific protocol and population. Other timing trials measure different outcomes, including stool communities; a metabolic improvement does not automatically imply a microbiome change.
step:living-well:fasting:2.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:fasting:3.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:fasting:3.text: As liver glycogen declines, the body relies more on fat and can produce more ketone bodies. There is no universal hour when everyone enters ketosis: food composition, activity and metabolic state matter. A ketogenic diet, fasting and taking a ketone supplement are distinct interventions.
step:living-well:fasting:3.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:fasting:4.subject: ketone-bodies
step:living-well:fasting:4.text: Ketogenic feeding changed stool communities in a human inpatient study. Follow-up cultures and mouse experiments tested ketone effects on bifidobacteria and intestinal immune cells. This offers a mechanism to investigate; it does not show that fasting-induced ketosis treats human gut inflammation.
step:living-well:fasting:4.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:fasting:5.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:fasting:5.text: In a small eight-week analysis in women with obesity, several measured sex hormones remained stable while DHEA decreased. Men were excluded, and menstrual-cycle ovarian hormones were not assessed before menopause. The study cannot establish fertility effects, long-term safety or an optimal fasting window for women.
step:living-well:fasting:5.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:fasting:6.subject: meal-timing
step:living-well:fasting:6.text: Direct comparisons between women and men remain scarce. Menstrual status, menopause, training load and adequate energy intake may influence responses. Current evidence does not justify fixed fasting hours by sex or menstrual phase. Male-only results and short female-only studies should both be read within their limits.
step:living-well:fasting:6.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:0.subject: toilet-posture
step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:0.text: Supporting the feet and leaning forward can make bowel emptying feel easier. In healthy volunteers, squatting reduced reported effort; in a constipation clinic, footstools did not improve a simulated evacuation test. Comfort, mobility and pelvic-floor function matter more than a single supposedly perfect posture.
step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:0.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:1.subject: anal-cleansing
step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:1.text: After passing stool, clean around the anus with gentle wiping, water or both, then pat dry. Avoid repeated scrubbing, strong fragrances and very hot water. This is care of the external skin: routine cleaning does not require flushing water into the rectum. Rectal irrigation for a bowel condition is a separate treatment taught by a clinician.
step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:1.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:2.subject: anal-cleansing
step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:2.text: Qualitative research in coastal Odisha found that water-based cleansing, privacy and daily routines shaped whether people used a toilet. A SuSanA practitioner survey describes variation across countries and between public, private, rural and urban settings. It is an exploratory account, not a representative map of religions or national habits.
step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:2.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:3.subject: anal-cleansing
step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:3.text: A Japanese convenience-sample survey documented electric-bidet habits and associations between some washing behaviours and itching. People may wash more because they already have symptoms, so the association does not establish cause. Water access, device design and mobility shape what feels practical; gentle cleaning is the aim.
step:living-well:toilet-posture-care:3.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:0.subject: cooking-method
step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:0.text: Stews and braises can make beans, vegetables and tougher cuts easier to prepare and chew. The digestive effect depends on the ingredient and its structure, not simply the clock. A small bean-meal experiment found different glucose responses after home boiling and commercial canning; it did not test a slow cooker.
step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:0.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:1.subject: cooking-method
step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:1.text: After a cooked white-bean meal, some starch reached the end of the small intestine enclosed within plant cell walls. This helps explain why a cooked pulse can still feed colonic microbes. Longer cooking can also increase starch accessibility: slower cooking does not automatically mean slower digestion or more resistant starch.
step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:1.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:2.subject: eating-pace
step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:2.text: Experiments that slowed eating generally reduced intake during that meal, without reliably changing later hunger. Chewing comfortably and pausing between bites may help you notice the meal and your appetite. These findings do not establish lasting weight loss, better nutrient absorption or a direct microbiome benefit.
step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:2.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.

step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:3.subject: cooking-method
step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:3.text: Try an unhurried meal and cook to a safe temperature rather than chasing a fixed number of hours. Slow-cooker safety depends on handling and heating. Raw dried kidney beans need proper soaking and high-temperature boiling; a low-temperature slow cooker alone may leave lectins active. Canned beans are a convenient already-cooked option.
step:living-well:slow-cooking-eating:3.limitations: This is an educational synthesis; read each finding for its experimental setting.
